properties.name: A claim about what the system IS carries when it was true, and is read back with its age
properties.statement: A statement about the system's CURRENT state must be recorded as a time-bounded assertion and surfaced with its age wherever it is read back, so it can go false. Prose written into a Requirement's `statement` has no expiry: it reads present-tense forever, no report flags it, and it is unfalsifiable by construction. The design already draws this line once — `dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap` ruled that a check older than its code is a freshness FACT rather than a gap — and this is the same distinction one node type along: a claim about what the design SHOULD BE belongs in Requirement prose; a claim about what the system IS RIGHT NOW belongs in a TemporalFact, which keeps both states instead of overwriting. Reading a dated observation back to a person as settled doctrine upgrades it into a standing property that nobody chose.
